title: An owner's hold on a mission source is a record the running integrator acts on: no task lands on it while held, its gates still run and their accepted tasks wait, assignment and every other source go on, and a forgotten hold expires by record and is told to the supervisor once
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, the module comment (the step list, "Every mission gets its step in every pass", "Gates run per mission, on threads"), `Integrator::pass_on` (the `moved` set: a landing ends its source's pass), `Integrator::mission` (the early `return land(...)` for a task in `landing`, which ends the mission's step before the baseline check and `objectives::assign_next`, `landing_elsewhere()`, the baseline check), `busy()`, `start_ready()`, the accepted branch of `judge_pushed` (the judging thread lands its own task), and `land()` (`spawn_landing_hold`, the compare-and-swap push, `stale` when main moved, a candidate already under main is a landing); `assign_next` in crates/spawn-cli/src/objectives.rs (its free slots are `workers` minus the mission's open tasks: a task waiting to land holds one); `spawn mission moved` and the usage in crates/spawn-cli/src/missions.rs; in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql `spawn_landing_hold` and `spawn_landing_release` (the advisory lock 1399957337), `spawn_mission_close` (a drop waits for that lock), `spawn_source_moved`, `spawn_integrator_record`, `spawn_control_record` (the store writes a host fault's `due_ms` into its record), `spawn_control_apply` (the `source.moved` case; an unknown record type raises), `spawn_control_refold()` and `spawn_now_ms()`; `MISSION_BOARD`, `GATED` and `STALL_FACTS` in crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs; crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch/stall.rs (the `landing` step, SPAWN_STALL_LANDING_SECS, and the halted mission's item, `session_id` `missions`), `Why`, `Escalation::tag` and `read_plan` in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs, `host_fault_escalations` in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch/digest.rs (a record told to the supervisor once); crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/attention.rs (`GET /api/attention`) and `missions()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`GET /api/missions`); deploy/deploy.sh (how the owner deploys; you may not edit it); rsi/backlog/021.json (owner pushes applied by the integrator; reported, not on main); docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 and docs/design.md §14.

The problem. An owner deploy of Spawn stalls every mission for about an hour. The owner deploys in two steps: gate a candidate against the live main with scripts/rsi/gate.sh and the RSI mission's scenarios directory (25-80 minutes), then run `deploy/deploy.sh <verdict>`, which refuses unless the verdict's base is still the live main. A landing during the gate makes the verdict stale: on 2026-11-06 at 21:45 task 85 (objective 18, a3543c2 on main) landed while the owner's gate ran, the owner's merge of the new main conflicted, and the gate had to run again. The only way to prevent it today is to stop spawn-integrate for the whole owner gate, with a timed restart as a fallback. That stops much more than landings on the Spawn source: every gate of every mission (killed with no record, as objective 021 measured: task 48 lost a 40-minute gate to a stop), and objective assignment, because `objectives::assign_next` runs only in the integrator: Supply PA's slice 8, six objectives pushed at 21:45, could not be assigned until the deploy finished. Objective 021 removes the stop for owner pushes; nothing stops landings while an owner gate judges against a fixed main. A hold is also not just a skipped push: today a task in `landing` ends its mission's step at once (no baseline check, no assignment, its source counted as moved for the rest of the pass), it keeps the other missions on its source from judging (`landing_elsewhere`), and the dispatcher escalates it after SPAWN_STALL_LANDING_SECS (600) as "the integrator lands it on its next pass". A task that waited there for an hour would stop its mission's assignment and its source's other gates, and tell the supervisor something false.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. Two owner commands. `spawn mission hold --source <source> [--reason <text>]` and `spawn mission release --source <source>`, owner login only (the supervisor's login is refused, as for `mission moved`). `<source>` is a mission source exactly as the missions name it (`spawn_source_allowed`, and the first source of at least one mission, whatever its state); a source no mission names, or a remote one (nothing lands there), is refused with exit 1 and nothing is recorded: a mistyped path must never look like a hold.
- hold: under the integrator's landing lock (`spawn_landing_hold`'s, 1399957337), so a landing whose compare-and-swap push has begun records its outcome first, it reads the source's main M and records `source.held` {`source`, `main`: M, `by`: `human`, `bound_s`, `reason` (when given, at most 500 characters)}; the store writes `expires_ms` into the record, its own `recorded_at_ms` + `bound_s` x 1000, as it writes a host fault's `due_ms`. `bound_s` is SPAWN_SOURCE_HOLD_SECS in the command's environment, default 10800 (3 h: longer than the slowest owner gate, 80 minutes, plus a deploy, and than the gate's default wall clock, 120 minutes), a whole number from 1 to 86400; any other value is refused (exit 1, naming the variable), never replaced by the default. It prints `{"hold": <the record's event id>, "source", "main", "expires_ms", "renews"}` and exits 0.
- two holds: a hold on a source already held renews it: a new `source.held` naming `renews` (the active hold's event id), with its own `main`, `bound_s` and `expires_ms`; the previous hold ends with it (no release or expiry is recorded for it), and its waiting tasks wait behind the new one. A source has at most one active hold. (`renews` is null on a hold that renews nothing.)
- release: records `source.released` {`source`, `hold`: the active hold's event id, `by`: `human`}, prints `{"source", "released": <that hold>, "waiting": [the tasks waiting behind it]}` and exits 0. With no active hold (never held, released, or expired) it records nothing, prints `{"source", "released": null, "waiting": []}` and exits 0, so a deploy that releases on every exit path never fails on it.
The fold keeps the active holds in a table keyed by source (`hold`, `main`, `by`, `reason`, `held_at_ms`, `expires_ms`), set by `source.held` and removed by the `source.released` or `source.hold_expired` naming its hold; `spawn_control_refold()` rebuilds it, and the dashboard's reader may read it.
2. While a source is held (from its `source.held` until a record ends the hold):
- no task lands on it. `land()` reads the hold from the store under the landing lock, before its push (never from memory): on a held source it pushes nothing. A candidate already in the source's main's history (a push from before the hold whose record was lost) is still recorded `task.landed`, as today: it landed before the hold. Any other records `task.held` {`id`, `hold`, `source`} once per task and hold (the store records nothing for a second one naming the same task and hold; `spawn_integrator_record` accepts it only for a task in `landing`; the fold sets the task's `held_by` to the hold), and the task stays `landing`. So a hold never splits a landing's push from its record;
- its gates still run (the judging threads, the wait for a gate slot, `stale`, `no_room`, `host_fault`, every verdict) and record their verdicts. An accepted task records `task.gated` `accepted` as today, then waits behind the hold (the judging thread's own `land()` records its `task.held`);
- a task waiting behind the hold ends nothing early: its mission's step goes on to the baseline check and `objectives::assign_next`, and its source is not counted as moved. The mission's other ready tasks wait behind it (one task per mission between its gate and its landing, as today); the other missions on the held source are judged as usual. A task whose `task.held` names the active hold is not a landing in flight: `landing_elsewhere()` ignores it (its `land()` pushed nothing, so main says nothing about it); a `landing` task without one still makes the other missions on its source wait, as today;
- assignment, the gates and landings of other sources, halts, budgets, `spawn mission moved` and owner pushes (objective 021's `spawn mission push`, when it exists: an owner landing is not a task landing) go on. The halt for a main moved with no record stays.
3. After the hold ends (its `source.released` or `source.hold_expired`), a waiting task lands at the integrator's next pass by the existing rules: when main moved meanwhile (an owner push, `spawn mission moved`), `land()` records `stale` and the task is judged again against the new main; it is never discarded and never counted.
4. The bound. At the start of each pass, before any mission's step, the integrator records `source.hold_expired` {`source`, `hold`, `expires_ms`, `waiting`: the ids of the tasks waiting behind it (still `landing`, `held_by` the hold), oldest first} for every active hold whose `expires_ms` the database's clock (`spawn_now_ms()`) has reached, whichever missions are on its source; the store refuses it for a hold that is not its source's active one, or before its `expires_ms`, so a release or renewal recorded first wins. Only that record ends the hold: past `expires_ms` without it nothing lands (the integrator lands on a held source only after a record ended the hold, never because time passed). A hold that expired while the integrator was down is recorded expired at its first pass, before anything lands. The dispatcher's digest takes each `source.hold_expired` to the supervisor once, as it takes 020's escalation: an item with `session_id` `missions` and id `source-hold-expired-<the record's event id>` (tag `missions source-hold-expired-<id>`), under a heading of its own ("a source hold expired"), whose line names the source, the hold (its event id, its `reason` when given, when it was taken and its bound), when it expired, each waiting task as `task #<id>` with its mission, and that landings on the source resumed (an owner verdict judged against the hold's `main` may be stale now: tell the owner). It is pending until a delivered digest carries its tag, whatever its age. A released hold is told to nobody.
5. Visible. `spawn mission list` and `GET /api/missions` (MISSION_BOARD) add `holds`: every active hold, `{source, hold, main, by, reason, held_at_ms, expires_ms, waiting: [the task ids waiting behind it, oldest first]}`; and each mission names `hold`: the event id of the active hold on its source, or null. `GET /api/attention` adds `holds`: the same entries, only those with at least one task waiting, beside `pending` and `told` and not among them (the supervisor is told of an expiry, never of a hold). The attention view and the Missions page show them (web/src), and `spawn task stages` shows the stage `held`. A task waiting behind a hold is not a landing stall: while its source is held its `landing` step is not escalated; after the hold ends the step is measured from the later of its accepted `task.gated` and the record that ended the hold.
6. The intended use (the owner's change; deploy/ is protected and out of scope): the owner takes the hold, gates the candidate against the hold's `main`, and deploy/deploy.sh releases it once main moved forward and `source.moved` is recorded, or on any failure; a hold forgotten or left by a crash expires by itself. Nothing in this objective stops or restarts spawn-integrate.
7. Causality (§14): the hold, the release and the expiry are records, and the integrator acts on them, read from the store under the landing lock before any push, never on timing or on an absence. The expiry's only use of time is the recorded `expires_ms` against the database's clock, and what ends the hold is the expiry's record, not the clock. Nothing depends on which loop ran first.
8. Independent of 021. This objective neither needs nor changes objective 021 (`spawn mission push`, `source.push_requested`, its step 0), which is reported and not on main, and 034.sh uses neither. If 021 is on main when this is solved, its owner landings are applied on a held source as on any other (its step 0 runs whatever the hold, and a held task's later landing finds main moved and is judged again, 021's (4)); if this lands first, nothing in a hold may stop 021's step 0 later. Both change the mission step and `spawn_integrator_record`, so the second to land may meet a textual conflict, never a semantic one.

State the rule in the module comment of integrate.rs (the step list: expired holds first; the landing step; "Every mission gets its step in every pass"), in docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 (Landing: the owner's hold), in docs/design.md §14 (所有者的改动: the hold is a record, and so is its end), and in the usage of `spawn mission`. Add unit tests in integrate.rs with a scratch source and mirror, as the landing tests do: `land()` on a held source pushes nothing, records one `task.held` (a second call records none) and leaves the task `landing`; a candidate already in main under a hold is recorded `task.landed`; a hold taken while a landing holds the landing lock waits for that landing's record and names the main it left; a mission step with a task waiting behind the hold still assigns an objective and does not mark the source moved; `landing_elsewhere` ignores a held task and still waits for a `landing` task without `task.held`; a judging on a held source records its verdict; after a release the task lands, and when main moved meanwhile it is `stale` and judged again; an expired hold is recorded before anything lands, once. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: the hold refuses a non-owner, a source no mission names, a remote source and a bad bound; the store writes `expires_ms`; a renewal names `renews` and ends the previous hold; a release with no hold records nothing; the expiry is refused before `expires_ms` and for a hold that is not active; `task.held` is refused for a task not in `landing` and recorded once per task and hold; the fold and the refold of the holds and of `held_by`. In the dispatcher: the expiry's item, its tag and line, told once; no landing stall while held, and the step measured from the hold's end after it. In serve: `holds` in /api/attention only while a task waits.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/034.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` (the Bridge, its pusher, the dispatcher, the supervisor, no model judge) runs `alpha` in objective mission A on source SA (accept = gate, `--workers 2`, a backlog the scenario writes) and `beta` in mission B on source SB (accept = gate, tasks assigned by the scenario), on a fake engine; one long-running `spawn integrate` (started once, never restarted) judges through a recording gate that accepts everything and holds a candidate holding beta2.txt until the scenario releases it; `spawn serve` answers GET /api/attention; the stall bounds are 1800 s except SPAWN_STALL_LANDING_SECS=10. It checks:
- (1) `spawn mission hold --source <SA>` prints a hold that is a `source.held` record naming SA, SA's main, `by` human and `expires_ms` = its own time + 10800000, and prints that main; then mission A gets objective 1 (alpha writes alpha.txt) and beta1 is assigned on SB; alpha's task is gated `accepted` while SA is held and beta1 lands on SB; over 12 s alpha's task stays `landing`, SA's main is the hold's, no `task.landed` names it, exactly one `task.held` names it and the hold (after its accepted verdict), and no mission halts; `spawn mission list` shows the hold in `holds` with alpha's task waiting, and as mission A's `hold` (B's is null); GET /api/attention lists it in `holds` with the task waiting, and no `stall-<task>-landing-*` item although the task has waited past the 10 s bound;
- (2) objective 2, added to the backlog, is assigned within 30 s while SA is still held;
- (3) `spawn mission release --source <SA>` prints `released` (the hold) and records `source.released` naming it; within 30 s alpha's task lands, after that record, and SA's main holds alpha.txt; the hold leaves the board; a second release exits 0 with `released` null and records nothing; a hold on a source no mission names is refused and records nothing;
- (4) while beta2's gate runs on SB, the owner holds SB with SPAWN_SOURCE_HOLD_SECS=20 (`expires_ms` = its time + 20000); released, beta2's gate records `accepted` and beta2 waits (`task.held` naming that hold); until `expires_ms` on the database's clock beta2 does not land, SB's main is the hold's and no expiry is recorded; within 30 s after it a `source.hold_expired` names the hold, SB and beta2 in `waiting`, recorded at or after `expires_ms`; beta2 lands after that record; within 60 s a digest tagged `missions source-hold-expired-<its event id>` reaches the supervisor with a line naming SB and task #<beta2>; 15 s later exactly one such digest was delivered in all, no mission ever halted, and the integrator is the same process.
On the live main (a3543c2) and the deployed binary (built from ffc9fe7) it fails at (1), 0.8-1.2 s after it starts: "(1) `spawn mission hold --source <SA>` exited 1: spawn: usage: ...". It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

What it saves. An owner deploy holds the Spawn source's landings for the owner gate's 25-80 minutes and nothing else: no gate of any mission or source is killed, objective assignment never waits (Supply PA's six objectives of 21:45 would have been assigned at the next pass, within about 5 s), and the owner's verdict stays on the live main, because no task lands under it (no repeat of 21:45). A task accepted on the held source lands at the first pass after the release; when the deploy moved main it is judged once more on the new main, the same gate it would have needed after a stop, without the gate the stop killed. A forgotten hold costs at most its bound (3 h by default) and reaches the supervisor once. On 017's scorecard this should improve throughput and lead time on every other source (no stop) and change no verdict on any work (first-pass quality and rework unchanged). None of the other objectives' scenarios may regress: 021.sh in particular keeps every check.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
